newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS - Kohl and Aznar had private chat about Euro.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Kohl and Aznar had private chat about Euro.

text.p: Germany's Chancellor Helmut Kohl and Spanish Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar discussed the European Union's planned single currency in a private talk late Tuesday, diplomatic sources in Bonn said on Wednesday.
Deputy spokesman for the German government Herbert Schmuelling said the meeting had been private and that he did not know what they spoke about.

Kohl is also due to meet Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi in Bonn on Thursday. The meetings have fuelled speculation Kohl might try to arrange a compromise allowing Spain and Italy to join the commmon European currency some time after it is launched in 1999.

EU officials say Italy and Spain have relatively slim chances of qualifying on all the Maastricht Treaty requirements for economic and monetary union (EMU) at the start despite their recent efforts to tighten fiscal controls.
Aznar flew to Germany at Kohl's invitation for dinner and talks that lasted over two-and-a-half hours in the German leader's homeland state of Rhineland-Palatinate.
They spoke about Madrid's efforts to rein in its budget deficit to try to qualify in time for the launch of the euro single currency, the diplomatic sources said.
Diplomatic sources said the two leaders spoke alone. Their entourage of government officals and diplomats sat at separate tables for dinner on Tuesday evening.
